{{Short description|In graph theory, edges incident/directed between the same vertices}}
[[Image:Multiple edges.png|thumb|Multiple edges joining two vertices.]]

In [[graph theory]], '''multiple edges'''  (also called '''parallel edges''' or a '''multi-edge'''), are, in an [[undirected graph]], two or more [[edge (graph theory)|edges]] that are [[incident (graph theory)|incident]] to the same two [[vertex (graph theory)|vertices]], or in a [[directed graph]], two or more edges with both the same tail vertex and the same head vertex. A [[simple graph]] has no multiple edges and no [[loop (graph theory)|loops]].

Depending on the context, a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] may be defined so as to either allow or disallow the presence of multiple edges (often in concert with allowing or disallowing loops):

*Where graphs are defined so as to ''allow'' multiple edges and loops, a graph without loops or multiple edges is often distinguished from other graphs by calling it a ''simple graph.''<ref>For example, see Balakrishnan, p. 1, and Gross (2003), p. 4, Zwillinger, p. 220.</ref>
*Where graphs are defined so as to ''disallow'' multiple edges and loops, a [[multigraph]] or a [[pseudograph]] is often defined to mean a "graph" which ''can'' have multiple edges.<ref>For example, see Bollobás, [https://books.google.com/books?id=SbZKSZ-1qrwC&pg=PA7 p. 7]; Diestel, [https://books.google.com/books?id=aR2TMYQr2CMC&pg=PA28 p. 28]; Harary, p. 10.</ref>

Multiple edges are, for example, useful in the consideration of [[electrical network]]s, from a graph theoretical point of view.<ref>Bollobás, [https://books.google.com/books?id=SbZKSZ-1qrwC&pg=PA39 pp. 39&ndash;40].</ref> Additionally, they constitute the core differentiating feature of [[multidimensional network]]s.

A [[planar graph]] remains planar if an edge is added between two vertices already joined by an edge; thus, adding multiple edges preserves planarity.<ref>Gross (1998), [https://books.google.com/books?id=CRDMgj-DfdEC&pg=PA308 p. 308].</ref>

A [[dipole graph]] is a graph with two vertices, in which all edges are parallel to each other.
